observations.output: tidepool scheduler drops jobs whose cron expression uses a step value like */7 in the minute field
parser in cron/expr.go splits on commas before slashes, so */7 becomes a literal star and the job never fires
step values now parse before list splitting and expand to every seventh minute, with a bounds check against 59
table test for step values in minute, hour and day-of-month fields including the */7 regression case
go test ./cron/... passed, opened PR #41 for cron step parsing in tidepool scheduler
tidepool worker pool leaks goroutines when a job context is cancelled mid-retry
retry loop in worker/run.go selects on the timer only and never on ctx.Done, so cancelled jobs sleep out the backoff
retry backoff now selects on ctx.Done as well, returns context.Canceled and releases the worker slot immediately
goleak-based test that cancels forty jobs mid-backoff and asserts no goroutines remain after shutdown
go test -race ./worker/... clean, goroutine count flat at 112 over a ten minute soak in the tidepool staging pod
add per-tenant concurrency limits to tidepool so one tenant cannot starve the queue
dispatcher in queue/dispatch.go pops jobs FIFO across all tenants with a single global semaphore of 64 slots
dispatcher keeps a weighted semaphore per tenant, default eight slots, read from the tenants table at startup
tenants table gains max_concurrency column with default 8 and a CHECK constraint between 1 and 64
load test with three tenants: noisy tenant capped at 8 running jobs, p99 queue wait for the others fell from 41s to 3s
tidepool job history table is 90GB and the dashboard query on it times out
history query in api/history.go filters on tenant_id and finished_at but the only index is on job_id
composite index on (tenant_id, finished_at DESC) created concurrently, and the query now pages by keyset instead of OFFSET
partition job_history by month with a retention job that drops partitions older than 180 days
dashboard history endpoint p95 went from 31s timeout to 140ms on the tidepool production replica
tidepool alerts fire twice for every failed job since the pager integration moved to webhooks
notifier/pager.go sends on both the legacy SMTP bridge and the new webhook, because the feature flag check was inverted
legacy SMTP bridge removed from notifier, webhook sender dedupes on job_id and attempt with a five minute window
notifier test asserts one webhook per failed attempt and none for retries that later succeeded
replayed yesterday's 212 failures through staging notifier, exactly 212 pages delivered and zero duplicates
move tidepool config from environment variables to a versioned YAML file with schema validation
config/load.go reads 31 TIDEPOOL_ environment variables with ad hoc strconv parsing and silent defaults
config loads tidepool.yaml validated against a JSON schema, env vars still override single keys for twelve factor deploys
JSON schema for tidepool.yaml covering queue, worker, tenants and notifier sections with required keys marked
tidepool config validate run against all four environment files, staging was missing notifier.webhook_url and now fails fast
tidepool graceful shutdown kills running jobs during a rolling deploy
main.go cancels the root context on SIGTERM without draining, and the pod terminationGracePeriodSeconds is only 30
SIGTERM now stops intake, waits up to 270s for running jobs to finish, then checkpoints the rest back to pending
deployment manifest sets terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 300 and a preStop sleep of five seconds for endpoint removal
rolling deploy during a 400 job burst finished with zero jobs killed and eleven checkpointed back to pending
tidepool metrics endpoint cardinality exploded after adding job name labels
metrics/jobs.go labels the duration histogram with job_name, which includes a per-run UUID suffix for ad hoc jobs
job_name label replaced by job_template, ad hoc runs collapse into one series, and run ids moved to exemplars
promtool unit test asserting the histogram stays under 500 series with ten thousand ad hoc runs
prometheus head series for tidepool fell from 1.9 million to 3,400 after the deploy, scrape time back under a second
kelpie build broke after a transitive serde_yaml minor release changed its error type
Cargo.toml lists serde_yaml = "0.9" so cargo update picked up 0.9.34 with the new error enum
kelpie config loader matches on the new serde_yaml error variants and keeps line and column in the message
cargo build and cargo test green on kelpie after the serde_yaml loader fix, PR #17 opened
kelpie sync command uploads the same chunk twice when the network drops mid-transfer
upload loop in src/sync.rs retries a chunk without checking whether the server already acknowledged its digest
kelpie sync asks the server for acknowledged digests before retrying and skips any chunk already stored
toxiproxy run dropping the link every 20s: 0 duplicate kelpie chunks across a 3GB upload, previously 41
kelpie progress bar flickers and corrupts the terminal on Windows Terminal
src/progress.rs redraws with raw carriage returns at 60Hz and ignores whether stderr is a terminal
kelpie progress output switched to indicatif with a 10Hz draw target and hidden when stderr is not a tty
manual check on Windows Terminal and on a piped CI log: kelpie progress renders cleanly and CI logs stay plain
kelpie restore is slow for archives with thousands of small files
restore in src/restore.rs fsyncs after every file and opens the index database once per entry
kelpie restore batches fsync per directory and holds one index transaction for the whole restore
restoring the 48k-file fixture archive dropped from 9m12s to 38s on the kelpie benchmark host
kelpie dependency bumps keep stalling because every exact pin needs a manual PR
Cargo.toml holds 27 exact = pins and renovate.json has every kelpie crate group disabled
Cargo.toml pins switched back to caret requirements and renovate groups the minor and patch bumps weekly
cargo update then cargo test on kelpie passed with the caret ranges, Cargo.lock regenerated and committed
kelpie prune deletes snapshots that are still referenced by a pinned tag
src/prune.rs builds the keep set from retention policy only and never reads the tags table
kelpie prune adds every snapshot reachable from a pinned tag to the keep set before applying retention
prune dry run on the staging repository now keeps the 6 tagged kelpie snapshots it used to delete

content: Rule for tidepool: never run schema migrations from the deploy hook. Run tidepool-migrate as its own Job and wait for it to finish before rolling out new pods.
Rule for kelpie: pin every dependency to an exact version (=1.2.3) in Cargo.toml. Caret ranges are not allowed.
Rule for kelpie, replacing the exact-pin rule: dependencies use caret ranges again with Cargo.lock committed, and renovate opens the weekly bumps.
